CLASS 10 · PHYSICS · CURRENT LAB

Make the current make sense.

Predict what will happen. Change the circuit. See why.

3 experiments · About 15 minutes
1 · Predict
2 · Experiment
3 · Check & reflect

BEFORE YOU TOUCH THE CIRCUIT

What do you think?

Two quick predictions. It’s fine to be unsure—these help you notice what changes in your understanding.

01
A fixed resistor carries 1 A at 6 V. What current would it carry at 12 V, at the same temperature?
A fixed resistor carries 1 A at 6 V. What current would it carry at 12 V, at the same temperature?
0.5 A
1 A
2 A
I’m not sure yet
02
You add an identical resistor in parallel across an ideal battery. What happens to the total current from the battery?
You add an identical resistor in parallel across an ideal battery. What happens to the total current from the battery?
It decreases
It stays the same
It increases
I’m not sure yet
Start student attempt →
Try without saving

Your latest five attempts, answers, progress and feedback are saved to your GTOP account and visible to GTOP admins. Starting another attempt replaces the oldest when five are saved. “Try without saving” sends no learning data.

THREE IDEAS. ONE CIRCUIT.

V
Voltage

Energy supplied per unit charge. Think of it as the electrical push.

volts (V)
I
Current

The amount of charge passing a point each second.

amperes (A)
R
Resistance

How much a component opposes current at a given voltage.

ohms (Ω)
The relationship you’ll discover
V = I × R
For an ohmic resistor at constant temperature.

CLASS 10 · PHYSICS · CURRENT LAB

Make the current make sense.

Predict what will happen. Change the circuit. See why.

1 · Predict
2 · Experiment
3 · Check & reflect

BEFORE YOU TOUCH THE CIRCUIT

What do you think?

Two quick predictions. It’s fine to be unsure—these help you notice what changes in your understanding.

01
A fixed resistor carries 1 A at 6 V. What current would it carry at 12 V, at the same temperature?
A fixed resistor carries 1 A at 6 V. What current would it carry at 12 V, at the same temperature?
0.5 A
1 A
2 A
I’m not sure yet
02
You add an identical resistor in parallel across an ideal battery. What happens to the total current from the battery?
You add an identical resistor in parallel across an ideal battery. What happens to the total current from the battery?
It decreases
It stays the same
It increases
I’m not sure yet
Start student attempt →
Try without saving

Your latest five attempts, answers, progress and feedback are saved to your GTOP account and visible to GTOP admins. Starting another attempt replaces the oldest when five are saved. “Try without saving” sends no learning data.

THREE IDEAS. ONE CIRCUIT.

V
Voltage

Energy supplied per unit charge. Think of it as the electrical push.

volts (V)
I
Current

The amount of charge passing a point each second.

amperes (A)
R
Resistance

How much a component opposes current at a given voltage.

ohms (Ω)
The relationship you’ll discover
V = I × R
For an ohmic resistor at constant temperature.
